title: Milestone evidence — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, a milestone contains code but no verification record. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud why code without a verification record does not close a milestone.

vocabulary.meaning: a milestone another person can check without asking the author, because its evidence travels with it
the reproducible trace showing that a claim was checked, as opposed to a statement that it works

expectedElements: The distinction between written and verified is made
The missing artefact is named precisely
A reproducible way to produce it is described
modelAnswer: The code is written, and that is not the same as the milestone being closed. What is missing is the part someone else can check without asking me: the command that runs, its output, and the assertion that would have failed before the change. Right now a reviewer has to take my word for it, which means the milestone is not reviewable, only visible. Producing it is not much work: the tests exist, they just are not recorded anywhere the reviewer can reach. I would attach the run output and the one test that proves the behaviour changed, which is the evidence a reviewer needs. Would that be enough for you to sign it off?
commonMistakes: Treating written code as sufficient evidence that a milestone is complete
Offering a screenshot in place of a reproducible command and its output
variants: Answer again when the reviewer has no environment to run the command in.
